derivation: Each value is an exact Decimal derivation from the quoted figures in the new sources (submissions.json) by the conventions in 'arithmetic'; nothing is read from code under test. Gap cells are spelled with the product's gap spelling; G# is bound at run time.

cell_notation.num_basis_points: unit basis_points is exact text plus ' bp' (report_view._UNIT_SUFFIX; no unit class): amount 50 shows '50 bp'
cell_notation.num: amount is the exact stored Decimal string; unit is the Fact unit; decimals is Fact.decimals; shown is the product spelling (display.py _number; report_view.fact_spelling): MULTIPLE shows the amount to `decimals` places with an x; decimal_fraction shows amount x 100 to `decimals` places with a percent sign; days, decisions and attributions are units with no class: exact text plus ' days' etc. (a count of one reads '1 decisions', cosmetic)
cell_notation.gap: status missing -> shown '∅ G#'; status not_applicable -> shown '∅ G# n.m.'; G# is bound at run time
cell_notation.value_class: source (quoted figure or verbatim quote), calculated (Python), analyst_judgment (label, process, basis, confidence, lessons, extra gaps, synthesis)
cell_notation.calculated_cites: a calculated fact carries the page-level cites of its inputs, or a calculation id when it has none
cell_notation.claims: text holds {fact_id|unit} figure references and [fact_id] gap chips only; resolved is the Python spelling; literal_text_outside_references holds no digit

arithmetic.decimal_context: the builder sets its decimal context explicitly: 28 significant digits, ROUND_HALF_UP, and the Inexact, InvalidOperation and DivisionByZero signals trapped, so any rounding fails the build; every stored value is an exact decimal (the only divisions are by 2 and by 100: mid = (bid + offer) / 2 / 100)
arithmetic.variance: variance = realized - expected, exact; direction is Higher if variance > 0, Lower if < 0, Unchanged if 0 (descriptive only: r14 step 4 assigns no cause and no favourable/adverse reading); magnitude = abs(variance), shown unsigned in the unit of the measure. A zero variance is a known 0.00x, not a missing value
arithmetic.multiples: total leverage and interest cover are quoted to two places and stored as MULTIPLE decimals 2 (1.67, 6.00, 1.80, 5.50)
arithmetic.loan_mid: (bid + offer) / 2 in points of par, then / 100 stored as decimal_fraction decimals 3: expected (98.50 + 99.25) / 2 = 98.875 -> 0.98875 shown 98.875%; realized (98.00 + 98.75) / 2 = 98.375 -> 0.98375 shown 98.375%; variance -0.00500 (a fraction of par); the magnitude is shown in basis points of par, abs(variance) x 10000 = 50 (unit basis_points, shown '50 bp'; review L2: 0.500 is points of par, the relative move is 0.506%, so the percent spelling was withdrawn); derived.loan_mid.magnitude keeps the fraction 0.00500 and magnitude_bp carries 50
arithmetic.observation_window: days = latest realized as-of date - decision date (calendar days): 2026-04-29 - 2026-01-10 = 109 (21 + 28 + 31 + 29); missing, never 0, when no realized observation exists. The latest as-of is the March 31 period end for the issuer figures and the April 29 quotation date; the run as-of (April 30) is not used
arithmetic.hit_rate: decisions labelled Thesis Confirmed / decisions whose overall label is not Insufficient Information; stored as a decimal fraction (decimals 1: positive 0 shown 0.0%, a known zero over one labelled decision); missing, never 0, when no decision carries a label other than Insufficient Information (the no-outcome case). The definition is this preparation's adaptation (r14 REF_CP-8_07 names the measure without a formula)
arithmetic.attribution_distribution: count of metric attributions (overall excluded) per label of the six-label taxonomy, unit attributions; every label has a row, so a zero count is a known 0 only when at least one metric was compared; with none compared the distribution is missing (T7.7 gap cell) and the stored derived.distribution and derived.by_direction are null, never 0 (review M4)
arithmetic.calibration_gate: decisions recorded = the count of Prior Case (decision record) sources in the pack, Python-counted (1 here: one source, one record); required = 3, a schema rule and r14 REF_CP-8_06 constant, not a calculation (its formula text says so; review L1); gate met only if recorded >= required, so it is never met here: target module, specific prior, supporting decisions and advisory recommendation are not_applicable (shown n.m.), never 0 and never a recommendation
arithmetic.module_status_cell: Completed only when no outcome_absence, all three measures are compared AND no realized entry is Interim; otherwise Completed with Limitations (r14 REF_CP-8_01: 'decision recorded but observation window still open - interim tracking only'). Every realized entry here is Interim, so both cases are Completed with Limitations (review H2). Blocked is never a head status here: a missing decision record is refused at begin through CP-0 (DO NOT RUN)
arithmetic.interim_final: r14 marks an entry interim whenever the closing of the observation window is not observable (not observable -> interim): no source type here states that a window is closed, so every row of T7.3 is Interim, the four observation rows, the default or restructuring row and the window, including a row with no realized entry (its value cells are gaps, its Interim cell is a known fact); Final never occurs here
arithmetic.downside_breach: a recorded downside size (thesis.downside_sizes: metric total_leverage or interest_cover, comparator above or below, level N.NN, each metric once, with a quote that is a span of the recorded downside paths and states '<measure> <comparator> <level>x') is breached when the realized figure is strictly beyond the level, decided by Python in Decimal: above -> realized > level, below -> realized < level; equal is not breached. derived.<metric>.downside_breach is true, false or null (null without a size or without a realized value; always null for loan_mid); T7.5 carries the calculated fact T7.5.<metric>.breach 'Breached' or 'Not breached' citing the size quote and the realized quote (a gap cell, not applicable, for loan_mid and overall). A Flagged Risk Materialized metric attribution needs a recorded size and breached true; an overall Flagged Risk Materialized needs at least one Flagged metric attribution with breached true (not checked when nothing is compared: the dedicated rule reports it). The analyst quotes the size; the comparison is not the analyst's
arithmetic.default_restructuring: T7.3 row from the issuer statement 'No default or restructuring has occurred as of April 30, 2026.' (update page:1), shown verbatim with its as-of date (the validator requires the quote to state default or restructuring, an issuer source, and a date after the decision); r14 SKILL.md Outcome Metrics 'Default / restructuring incidence' (review M3). Missing (never 'none occurred') when no outcome source exists

tamper.case: positive (closed run: CP-0 and CP-8 settled, receipt sealed)
tamper.why_this_fact: the direction is Python-derived (variance sign) and lives only in the settled CP-8 result Module; the step output holds the submission references and no direction, and the table cell is in the Module. It is the one fact the probe's rebuild (derive over the journaled payload) contradicts. Frozen CP-DR recipe (docs/CPDR-OWNER-LEASE.md Tamper; cases/cpdr-owner/expected.json tamper) applied to this fact
recipe: 1. Copy the closed positive store directory (blobs, snapshots, current, audit) to a scratch path.

2. Load the CP-8 head's result Module; replace only the text of fact T7.4.total_leverage.direction (Higher -> Lower); leave every other fact (including T7.4.total_leverage.magnitude and the cp8.what_changed lines), table, claim and limitation unchanged.
3. Serialise the forged Module as Execution._store does (model_dump_json); its sha256 R2 must equal Module.content_hash(); write blobs/R2.

4. Build a new ExecutionSnapshot equal to the current one with the CP-8 Attempt.result_sha256 and Head.result_sha256 set to R2 (status, inputs and commands unchanged, so head_of(forged Module) equals the Head) and the same parent; write snapshots/<its sha256>.json and rewrite current to that digest.

5. In the retained receipt: set the CP-8 SettledHead.result_sha256 to R2; set receipt.snapshot_sha256 and every coordinate that named the old final snapshot (the CP-8 settling OwnerSubmission.snapshot_after_sha256: owner_workflow.py _advance -> _finish_walk; its record is retained as audit/submissions/<content_hash> by _retain) to the new digest; delete audit/submissions/<old record hash> and write the edited OwnerSubmission as audit/submissions/<its content_hash> (model_dump_json bytes); rewrite audit/receipt.sha256 with the forged receipt's content_hash (S1a R3-5 and CP-3 A4 pattern: the audit file travels under its new hash).

expect.passes: everything upstream of the probe: _verify_audit (owner_workflow.py:802-830) and every check before _PROBES (audit inventory, blob and snapshot hashes, ancestor walk, head_of equality, begin and publication records, call and read replay, journaled-step replay: the payload and step are untouched)
expect.refuses: cp8.probe raises WorkflowError('identity_mismatch') (reached through _PROBES[head.module_id], owner_workflow.py:1182); verify_owner_run_receipt raises identity_mismatch
expect.test_asserts: on the forged copy _verify_audit and every check before _PROBES pass; then cp8.probe raises identity_mismatch. Asserting identity_mismatch alone would not show that the probe was reached.

tamper.step_output_edit: an edited CP-8 step output (or payload blob) is caught by the store's own blob hash check, not by the probe's output comparison (recorded limitation, S1a R3-5); this is why the target is a Module fact and not the step output
